question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I first read the supplied guide to learn the permitted recorder workflow. I requested the installed vocabulary collection to locate the canonical C# body-kinds path, then read that vocabulary in HAL to find its value count and the two native IDs. Because the initial value list gave no individual definitions, I made one focused request selecting those two IDs to check whether their entries carried more detail and to inspect the selected-response scope. It showed BreakStatement's display name and confirmed that completeness applied only to the selected values. At that point the catalog established the identities, count, body-query role, and omission semantics. Further catalog reads were unlikely to add definitions, so I answered with a clearly identified interpretation of the C# syntax-kind names.
